title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
summary: A critical security flaw was found in the binary-parser library that could let attackers run malicious code. This affects versions before 2.3.1.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything. If you are a developer or your workplace uses software containing the binary-parser library, your technical team will need to update it.
action_it: Update the binary-parser library to version 2.3.1 or later to fix the code injection vulnerability.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical security flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect software. This vulnerability allows attackers to run malicious software on technicians' computers without warning.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses ConnectWise ScreenConnect, your IT team should already be on it.
action_it: Apply the vendor patch for CVE-2026-84869 immediately and check systems for signs of unauthorized access.

title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
summary: N-able discovered a critical security flaw in its Mail Assure email filtering service while investigating a breach. This vulnerability could allow a user with high-level access to connect to internal systems.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses N-able Mail Assure, your IT team should handle the necessary updates.
action_it: Review the N-able disclosure regarding CVE-2026-134624 and apply any available patches or mitigations provided by the vendor for the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical security flaw in an old ASP.NET library called Idunno.AntiCsrf. This flaw allows attackers to remotely run harmful code on vulnerable systems without needing a password.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you build or manage software at your workplace, check if your systems use this legacy library.
action_it: Discontinue using and remove the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library immediately, as researchers advise against further use of the abandoned software.

title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials
summary: An exploited security flaw in Microsoft Azure allowed attackers to steal stored API credentials from customers. Norwegian authorities linked the issue to cyberattacks targeting energy companies.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Microsoft Azure services, your IT team should already be investigating potential impacts.
action_it: Review Azure API Management Classic tier deployments for signs of unauthorized access, and rotate any potentially compromised API credentials or secrets.

title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
summary: Hackers exploited a security flaw in GL.iNet's cloud management service to install malware on customer routers and KVM devices. The vendor has fixed the flaw and blocked the attackers' access.

also_covered.title: Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace or home uses GL.iNet routers or KVM devices, the company has already fixed the cloud flaw, but you should check your devices for any unauthorized changes.
action_it: Review affected GL.iNet routers and KVM devices for signs of unauthorized access, custom malware, backdoors, or reverse shells since the cloud flaw has now been patched by the vendor.

title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
summary: Three artificial intelligence hosting companies leaked sensitive customer prompts and secrets for months without realizing it. The gateway service OpenRouter has dropped these providers from its platform.

also_covered.title: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets

title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
summary: Hackers stole personal information from soccer fans who used services provided by Spain's LaLiga and some affiliated clubs. This matters because exposed personal data can be used by criminals for identity theft or targeted scams.

title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards
summary: Hackers breached the B2B top-up provider GlobeTopper, stealing $70,000 in gift cards and causing $2.5 million in lost revenue. The attack disrupted normal business operations.

title: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops
summary: Microsoft is testing a fix for a long-standing Windows 11 bug that causes poor audio quality when using Bluetooth headphones. Fixing this issue will restore clear sound for users who experience sudden drops in audio performance.

title: Microsoft confirms Windows printing issues affecting Forcepoint users
summary: A recent Microsoft Windows update is causing printing problems for computers using Forcepoint data protection software. This issue only impacts devices running that specific software after installing the November 2026 update.

title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access
summary: A threat group called Webworm is using a modified version of the SoftEther VPN tool to hide remote access into compromised networks. This matters because it allows attackers to maintain secret access while evading security detection.

title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and a Whole Lot of Shell Trouble
summary: This week's security recap highlights various cyber threats, including a VMware zero-day vulnerability and multiple code execution flaws. These incidents demonstrate how attackers exploit routine updates and existing access points to compromise systems.

title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap
summary: AI agents operating across multiple platforms create security gaps because no single vendor can control their actions. Organizations must better manage agent identities and permissions to close these accountability holes.

title: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans
summary: A Peruvian call center operator was sentenced to eight years in prison for participating in a scheme that stole millions of dollars from tens of thousands of Spanish-speaking U.S. residents. The criminals used government impersonation tactics to trick victims into handing over money.
